os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session
app: Cursor 2.x (VS Code fork, Electron/Chromium 144) — isolated instance, temp profile

stack_detection.method: open debug port answers /json/version; Electron flag pass-through
stack_detection.signature: http://127.0.0.1:9224/json/version → Chrome/144.0.7559.236; app warns 'remote-debugging-port is not in the list of known options, but still passed to Electron/Chromium'

channel_setup: Launch binary with --remote-debugging-port=9224 --user-data-dir=<short path>. Two real-world traps hit: (1) the app SILENTLY dies if user-data-dir exceeds the 103-char unix-socket limit (listen EINVAL on its single-instance socket) — a launch-orchestration failure mode, not a channel failure; (2) like Chrome, the port exists only if the app was launched with it — the user's running VS Code was NOT probeable via CDP without restarting it (declined: it was in active use).

t1_read_text.detail: Workbench UI text read exactly from the DOMSnapshot distillation: menu items with keyboard shortcuts ('New Agent ⌘N', 'Search ⌘K'), section headers, repo names. Pre-login the same probe honestly returned only the 3-line login gate (218 B) — the channel reports what is on screen, gated content stays gated.

t2_enumerate.detail: 17 interactive elements with aria-labels and boxes (Hide Sidebar, Go Back/Forward, Open Workspace, Settings, 'Update: restart Cursor to install'…). Electron apps carry their own ARIA annotations — the DOM view inherits them for free.

t3_live_value.detail: Not run — no safe writable field on this screen without triggering agent/workspace actions in the user's account; channel identical to the Chrome cell where T3 passed.

t4_living_screen.detail: Idle workbench re-snapshots: 0,0,0 diff bytes across 3 s — a static Electron UI costs nothing to watch; capture 15 ms.

t5_blind_action.detail: Skipped deliberately: every clickable on this screen mutates account state (agents, workspace). Blind-click mechanics for CDP proven in macos-chrome-cdp (device-px vs CSS-px DPR trap applies identically here: boxes are DPR=2 device px).

t6_pictorial.detail: No canvas/image region on the workbench start screen; nothing to declare.

measurements.notes: Logged-in 'Cursor Agents' window, 1280×800-CSS-ish viewport (dpr 2 → screenshot at device px would be 5464 tokens). The distilled view (56 lines) is 2.1× cheaper than one CSS-resolution screenshot and self-labels every control via aria-label — no vision pass needed to name buttons. Login-gated content is an honest boundary: pre-login view was 218 B with exactly the two buttons that existed.

runtime_verification.method: CDP screenshot of the same instant kept as artifact; text/controls compared against the distilled view.
runtime_verification.agreement: Full agreement on visible content; no fabricated content observed in either state (pre/post login).

permissions_required: None (loopback CDP). The user chose to log the probe instance into their Cursor account; the temp profile (containing the auth token) was deleted after the probe.
